signals.entity: Magyar Nemzeti Bank (MNB) - designated EAA market-surveillance authority for ATMs and payment terminals
signals.signal: Government Decree 605/2022 (XII.28.) designates the MAGYAR NEMZETI BANK (the central bank) itself as the market-surveillance authority under Hungary's EAA transposition (Act XVII of 2022, 'Aktv') for payment terminals and ATMs connected to payment services, and for consumer banking services. The penalty framework in Sec.9 of the decree is far heavier than previously recorded: minimum HUF 15,000; for LARGE enterprises (annual revenue above HUF 100m, non-SME) up to 5% OF ANNUAL NET REVENUE capped at HUF 500 MILLION; up to HUF 500,000 for smaller undertakings, or 5% of revenue where serious consumer harm arises. Transitional rules mirror the Directive: terminals put into use before 28/06/2025 may run to the end of their economically useful life, maximum 20 years from deployment; services may keep using pre-existing products until 28/06/2030; 112 emergency-call accessibility from 28/06/2027.
signals.source_name: Nemzeti Jogszabalytar (Hungarian consolidated law database) - 605/2022. (XII. 28.) Korm. rendelet, and 2022. evi XVII. torveny (Aktv)
signals.implies: (a) AFFECTED: OTP, MBH, Erste Hungary, K&H, CIB, Raiffeisen Hungary, UniCredit Hungary, Granit, MagNet - i.e. the whole Hungarian ATM/POS-owning banking sector, supervised on accessibility by their own prudential regulator. (b) MUST BUY/CHANGE: EAA/EN 301 549-conformant ATM and POS hardware and UI - audio guidance + headphone jack, tactile keys, contrast/large-font screens, reachable card/cash apertures - plus terminal-management (TMS) proof of configuration; maps to Printec NCR ATM supply and x-core multivendor accessible UI, Verifone/Castles accessible POS + TMS, and field services. (c) BUDGET: because the supervisor is the MNB rather than a consumer agency, accessibility findings land in the same supervisory dialogue as prudential/payments matters - remediation budget should be committed in the 2026/2027 cycle.
signals.likelihood: High that MNB folds accessibility checks into routine payments supervision within 6-12 months
signals.followup: CORRECTS the baseline (which recorded 'Hungary up to ~HUF 30m'): the statutory ceiling is 5% of net revenue capped at HUF 500m for large enterprises. Check MNB's supervisory publications/piacfelugyelet page for any accessibility decision naming a bank.

signals.entity: Magyar Nemzeti Bank - MNB Regulation 19/2025 (VI.26.) mandatory ATM rollout
signals.signal: MNB Regulation 19/2025 (VI.26.) sets the criteria and the bank-by-bank allocation for a state-mandated ATM installation programme in settlements with no cash-withdrawal point, and names nine obliged payment service providers: OTP Bank, MBH Bank, Erste Bank Hungary, K&H, CIB, Raiffeisen Bank, UniCredit Bank Hungary, Granit Bank and MagNet Bank; banks may contractually transfer the obligation to one another and a successor must reimburse the predecessor's installation costs incurred within 3 years. Hungarian financial press (Penzcentrum, 27/06/2025) reports the programme totals 1,039 new ATMs, with settlements above 1,000 inhabitants to be served by 31/12/2025 and settlements above 500 inhabitants by 31/12/2026, based on 2022 census population. CRITICAL INTERACTION: every one of these machines is placed into service AFTER 28/06/2025, so none benefits from the EAA legacy-fleet derogation - each must be accessibility-conformant on day one.
signals.source_name: Nemzeti Jogszabalytar - 19/2025. (VI. 26.) MNB rendelet [MNB Regulation on the criteria for installing automated banknote dispensing machines and cost-sharing among payment service providers]; volume/deadline figures from Penzcentrum
signals.implies: (a) AFFECTED: the nine named Hungarian banks, with OTP and MBH carrying the largest allocations. (b) MUST BUY/CHANGE: roughly a thousand NEW ATMs - typically low-footprint, remote-managed, off-branch units - all of which must be EAA-conformant from installation and all of which need remote monitoring, cash forecasting and field service in low-density rural locations. This is the single most concrete ATM hardware+service tender pool in the footprint and maps to Printec NCR ATM supply, ATM telemetry/monitoring, NCR APTRA OptiCash cash optimisation (rural replenishment economics are brutal without it), physical ATM security, and managed/field services (500+ engineers). (c) BUDGET: the 31/12/2026 tranche means procurement and installation contracts must already be running in H2-2026 - this is a NOW decision, not a future one.
signals.likelihood: Very high - the obligation is in force and bank-specific; the 31/12/2026 tranche is 5 months away
signals.followup: Verify against the MNB rendelet annex how many machines fall in the 500-999 inhabitant tranche and which banks carry them; confirm whether the 31/12/2025 tranche was delivered on time (press dates in jogtar's consolidated text show 31/07/2025 and 16/03/2026 as contract/assignment milestones - these are NOT the same as the installation deadlines, so re-verify both before quoting). Approach OTP and MBH procurement plus Erste/Raiffeisen/UniCredit Hungary; pitch rural ATM as a managed service.

signals.entity: Hrvatska narodna banka (HNB) and HANFA - accessibility supervisors for consumer banking services
signals.signal: Croatia's EAA transposition, the Zakon o zahtjevima za pristupacnost proizvoda i usluga, was published in Narodne novine 89/2025 on 13/06/2025 and entered into force 28/06/2025. Art.25(7) assigns market surveillance of CONSUMER BANKING SERVICES accessibility to the HRVATSKA NARODNA BANKA (Croatian National Bank) and HANFA; Art.22(3) assigns product-side inspection of non-radio products (which includes self-service terminals/ATMs) to the market inspectors of the Drzavni inspektorat (State Inspectorate). Fines are far higher than previously recorded: EUR 6,630 to EUR 132,720 for legal persons, both for service providers (Art.36(1)) and for producers/authorised representatives of self-service terminals (Arts.32/33), plus EUR 2,650-6,630 personally on the responsible person in the legal entity. Art.37(3) carries the legacy derogation: self-service terminals lawfully in use before 28/06/2025 may continue to the end of economic life, maximum 20 years from first use.
signals.source_name: Narodne novine 89/2025, Zakon o zahtjevima za pristupacnost proizvoda i usluga [Act on accessibility requirements for products and services]
signals.implies: (a) AFFECTED: Zagrebacka banka (UniCredit), PBZ (Intesa), Erste&Steiermarkische (an existing Printec OptiCash customer), OTP Croatia, RBA Croatia, HPB. (b) MUST BUY/CHANGE: accessible ATM/POS estate and accessible digital channels, evidenced to a prudential regulator (HNB) rather than a consumer agency - meaning documented EN 301 549 conformance assessments, not just retrofits; maps to Printec NCR ATM refresh, x-core accessible multivendor UI, Glory/Sesami TCR and kiosk deployments, POS + TMS. (c) BUDGET: with HNB in the enforcement seat and a EUR 132,720 per-breach ceiling, Croatian banks should be committing accessibility remediation capex in the 2026/2027 budget.
signals.likelihood: High that HNB raises accessibility in 2026/2027 supervisory dialogue; enforcement decisions not yet published
signals.followup: CORRECTS the baseline figure of 'Croatia EUR 2k-50k' - the legal-person range is EUR 6,630-132,720. Check hnb.hr and dirh.gov.hr for any published accessibility supervisory expectation or inspection results; lead with the Erste Croatia relationship.

signals.entity: Ceska obchodni inspekce (CTIA) - Czech Trade Inspection Authority
signals.signal: Czechia enforces the EAA through Act No. 424/2023 Sb. (effective 28/06/2025), with the CTIA as the principal supervisory body for products (including self-service terminals and ATMs) and for e-commerce and other in-scope services; CTU supervises electronic communications, the Ministry of Transport and regional authorities transport services. Sec.22/24 of the Act require supervisory bodies to PUBLISH ON THEIR WEBSITES a list of products and services in their supervisory scope - CTIA maintains this as a downloadable register. FIRST OBSERVED ENFORCEMENT: in its Q1-2026 targeted internet-sales inspection round (123 inspections, breaches found in 97 = 78.86%), CTIA folded in checks of accessibility duties under Act 424/2023 and identified 6 breaches of that Act, mostly resolved by remedial orders rather than fines. Self-service and payment terminals a provider began using by 27/06/2025 may run to end of life, maximum 20 years from first commissioning.
signals.source_name: Ceska obchodni inspekce - 'Pristupnost vyrobku a sluzeb' business and consumer pages (supervisory role, published register); Q1-2026 inspection figures reported from CTIA's quarterly internet-sales release
signals.implies: (a) AFFECTED: Ceska sporitelna (Erste), CSOB (KBC), Komercni banka (SG), Moneta, Raiffeisenbank CZ, UniCredit CZ, and independent ATM deployers. (b) MUST BUY/CHANGE: CTIA has moved from guidance to actual inspection and is naming non-compliant products/services publicly - a reputational as well as financial exposure. Banks need EN 301 549 conformance evidence for terminals and accessible ATM UI; maps to Printec NCR ATM refresh, x-core accessible UI, kiosks, POS/TMS. (c) BUDGET: CTIA's first accessibility findings are e-commerce, but terminals are explicitly in its product scope - budget for terminal conformance assessment and UI remediation in 2027 planning, decided in H2-2026.
signals.likelihood: Medium-High that CTIA extends targeted accessibility inspections from e-commerce to self-service terminals within 12 months
signals.followup: Download CTIA's published Sec.22/24 register (Excel) and check whether any ATM/payment-terminal product or bank service is listed; pull CTIA's 2025 annual report (Zaverecny ucet, Feb-2026) for accessibility inspection resourcing. Baseline recorded a CZK 2m ceiling - not re-verified this run against the Act text; treat as unconfirmed.

signals.entity: Banka Slovenije
signals.signal: Ahead of the 28/06/2025 application date of Slovenia's EAA transposition (Zakon o dostopnosti do proizvodov in storitev za invalide, ZDPSI), BANKA SLOVENIJE formally notified payment service providers established in Slovenia of the statutory accessibility requirements and CALLED ON THEM TO PRESENT THEIR PLANNED APPROACHES to making their services accessible, saying it would encourage adoption of good practice. The law covers computer hardware and operating systems, ATMs, payment terminals and ticket machines, and e-banking/mobile apps. Accessibility readiness among Slovenian banks was reported as highly uneven - 'from those close to accessible solutions, to those still very far' (accessibility expert Tilen Skraba).
signals.source_name: RTV Slovenija, 'Smo pripravljeni na izvajanje Zakona o dostopnosti do proizvodov in storitev za invalide?' [Are we ready to implement the Act on accessibility of products and services for people with disabilities?]
signals.implies: (a) AFFECTED: NLB, NKBM/OTP Slovenia, SKB (OTP), UniCredit Slovenia, Intesa Sanpaolo Bank Slovenia, Delavska hranilnica. (b) MUST BUY/CHANGE: a documented, plan-based accessibility roadmap for ATMs and payment terminals that the central bank has explicitly asked to see - this is a procurement-shaped request, not a legal abstraction; maps to Printec accessibility gap-assessment + x-core accessible ATM UI + NCR ATM/recycler refresh + kiosk deployments, sold as a roadmap Banka Slovenije will accept. (c) BUDGET: the central bank has already asked for plans; capex should sit in the 2026/2027 budget.
signals.likelihood: High - the supervisor has asked for plans, so banks must show funded roadmaps
signals.followup: Obtain Banka Slovenije's actual communication to PSPs (bsi.si) and confirm whether it has since published expectations or a follow-up review; verify ZDPSI fine levels from the Uradni list text - not established this run.

signals.entity: Sozialministeriumservice (Austrian market-surveillance authority for BaFG)
signals.signal: One year after the EAA (European Accessibility Act, Directive (EU) 2019/882) became applicable on 28/06/2025, the Austrian market-surveillance authority Sozialministeriumservice had opened 84 proceedings under the Barrierefreiheitsgesetz (BaFG), of which 74 were still pending and 36 were opened ex officio; 22 of the pending proceedings concern BANKING SERVICES specifically, and 53 self-notifications of non-conformity by companies came predominantly from banking and finance/insurance. No administrative fine had yet been imposed - the authority is running a 'Beraten vor Strafen' (advise before penalise) policy, with a ceiling of EUR 80,000 (EUR 50,000 micro/SME) available for persistent breaches. The BaFG explicitly covers 'Selbstbedienungsterminals wie Bankomaten' (self-service terminals such as ATMs) and payment terminals placed on the market after 28/06/2025.
signals.source_name: Oesterreichischer Behindertenrat, 'Ein Jahr Barrierefreiheitsgesetz: Die Umsetzung hat begonnen' [One year of the Accessibility Act: implementation has begun], corroborated by the Sozialministeriumservice BaFG market-surveillance page
signals.implies: (a) AFFECTED: every Austrian retail bank running an ATM/payment-terminal estate - Erste/Sparkassen, RBI, BAWAG, Bank Austria, Raiffeisen regional banks. (b) MUST BUY/CHANGE: accessibility-conformant ATM hardware and software - audio guidance with 3.5mm headphone jack, tactile keypad, screen-contrast/large-font UI, wheelchair reach - plus a multivendor UI layer to retrofit mixed fleets; maps to Printec NCR ATM refresh, x-core multivendor ATM software with accessible UI templates, self-service kiosks, and managed/field services for retrofit rollout. (c) BUDGET: the advise-before-penalise grace is visibly ending - with 22 live banking proceedings, remediation capex should be committed in the 2026/2027 cycle now.
signals.likelihood: High that Austrian banks commission accessibility retrofits/UI upgrades within 6-12 months; first administrative fines plausible in that window
signals.followup: Ask Sozialministeriumservice (or watch its next market-surveillance report) for the sectoral breakdown and whether any ATM-specific decision has issued; approach Erste/RBI/BAWAG accessibility programme owners with an x-core accessible-UI retrofit proposition.

signals.entity: Raiffeisen Bank Romania
signals.signal: Raiffeisen Bank Romania publishes a public accessibility statement referencing Legea 232/2022 (the Romanian EAA transposition) committing that 'by the end of 2025, ATMs and MFMs (multifunctional machines) in the fleet will have the new specific accessibility functionality implemented' - audio-guided cash withdrawal and balance enquiry, use of personal headphones, and symbols in relief on the machine. Cards for individuals carry Braille markings since 15/05/2024; the website is stated to comply with WCAG 2.1 level AA. This is a footprint bank publicly binding itself to an ATM-fleet accessibility retrofit. Romanian fines under Legea 232/2022 are contraventional and modest (roughly 2,500-15,000 lei depending on the breach), but supplementary measures include product withdrawal/recall and suspension of the activity or authorisation for the period of non-compliance - which is the real risk for a bank.
signals.source_name: Raiffeisen Bank Romania - Accesibilitate [Accessibility] statement; fines/supplementary measures corroborated from Legea 232/2022 commentary (JURIDICE.ro)
signals.implies: (a) AFFECTED: Romanian banks with large ATM/MFM estates - Raiffeisen, BCR (an existing Printec APTRA customer), BRD, Banca Transilvania, UniCredit, CEC Bank. (b) MUST BUY/CHANGE: ATM audio-guidance software plus headphone-jack-equipped hardware, tactile/relief keypads and symbols, accessible screen flows on deposit/recycling MFMs; maps directly to Printec NCR ATM supply including intelligent-deposit/recycling, x-core multivendor accessible UI, and field services for a fleet-wide retrofit. (c) BUDGET: Raiffeisen has already committed; peer banks that have not must commit in the 2026 cycle - suspension of activity is a disproportionate consequence relative to the small fine, so boards move on it.
signals.likelihood: High - a named footprint bank has committed publicly; peer follow-through likely within 6-12 months
signals.followup: Confirm with Raiffeisen Romania whether the end-2025 ATM/MFM accessibility milestone was actually delivered fleet-wide and who supplied it; use as a reference with BCR and Banca Transilvania. Baseline's correction stands: enforcement is ANPC + ANPD/ADR, NOT ANCOM.

signals.entity: Bulgarian Parliament / State Agency for Metrological and Technical Supervision (DAMTN)
signals.signal: Bulgaria's EAA transposition, the Zakon za iziskvaniyata za dostapnost na produkti i uslugi [Act on Accessibility Requirements for Products and Services], was promulgated in Darjaven Vestnik (State Gazette) issue 31 of 11/04/2025. Art.2(1)(2) expressly covers self-service terminals including 'terminalni ustroystva ATM' and payment terminals. Art.34(1) names the CHAIR OF DAMTN (State Agency for Metrological and Technical Supervision) as the market-surveillance authority for products - not the Consumer Protection Commission and not the BNB. Sanctions: Art.73(1) fine BGN 1,000-5,000 on natural persons or a property sanction of BGN 5,000-25,000 on companies placing non-compliant products on the market, doubling to BGN 2,000-10,000 / BGN 10,000-50,000 on repeat; Art.87 fine BGN 1,000-10,000 / property sanction BGN 2,000-15,000 for service providers failing to supply required accessibility information. Transitional rules: service providers may keep using previously lawful products until 28/06/2030; self-service terminals lawfully in use before 28/06/2025 may run up to 20 years from first deployment; emergency-call requirements bite 28/06/2027.
signals.source_name: Darjaven Vestnik (Bulgarian State Gazette), Zakon za iziskvaniyata za dostapnost na produkti i uslugi, DV br.31/11.04.2025
signals.implies: (a) AFFECTED: all Bulgarian banks and acquirers with ATM/POS estates - UniCredit Bulbank, DSK (OTP), UBB (KBC), Postbank, Fibank, plus Borica as national processor. (b) MUST BUY/CHANGE: any NEW ATM or payment terminal placed on the market must be EAA-conformant on day one (EN 301 549), and the 28/06/2030 service-provider cut-off caps how long legacy screens/UIs can stay; maps to Printec NCR ATM replacement/recycler programmes, Verifone/Castles accessible POS + TMS, and x-core accessible UI. (c) BUDGET: Bulgaria's euro changeover (01/01/2026) already forced an ATM/POS software and cash-handling refresh - the 28/06/2030 accessibility cut-off means that fleet decision should be taken ONCE; budget must commit 2026-2028, i.e. now, to avoid a second touch of every machine.
signals.likelihood: High that Bulgarian banks combine euro-changeover fleet work with accessibility conformance in 2026-2028; DAMTN enforcement against banks not yet observed
signals.followup: Refines the baseline (which recorded only BGN 1,000-5,000 / BGN 10,000 repeat and did not identify DAMTN): the corporate property sanction runs to BGN 25,000, BGN 50,000 on repeat. Check DAMTN's inspection plan and sanction register for any 2026 self-service-terminal action; note BGN amounts convert at the fixed euro rate post 01/01/2026.

signals.entity: Deputy Ministry of Social Welfare (Cyprus)
signals.signal: Cyprus transposed the EAA via the Accessibility of Products and Services Law of 2024, announced 02/05/2024, with the Deputy Ministry of Social Welfare as the competent authority for oversight and complaints. Requirements apply from 28/06/2025 to payment terminals and self-service terminals such as ATMs, ticketing and check-in machines and interactive information terminals; self-service terminals lawfully used before 28/06/2025 may continue to the end of their economic life but no later than 20 years, i.e. an absolute backstop of 28/06/2045. No Cypriot enforcement action against a bank or ATM operator has been published as of 02/08/2026.
signals.source_name: AccessibleEU (European Commission centre), 'Cyprus announces the Accessibility of Products and Services Law of 2024'
signals.implies: (a) AFFECTED: Bank of Cyprus (an existing Printec Glory TCR customer), Hellenic Bank/Eurobank Cyprus, Alpha Bank Cyprus, Astrobank, plus Euronet. (b) MUST BUY/CHANGE: accessible ATM and TCR/kiosk user interfaces and any new terminal placed after 28/06/2025 must conform on day one; maps to Printec Glory/Sesami TCR and kiosk deployments (already a live Bank of Cyprus relationship), NCR ATM refresh and x-core accessible UI. (c) BUDGET: absent visible enforcement, the driver is the branch-transformation/TCR cycle rather than a fine - attach accessibility conformance to the next TCR/kiosk tranche rather than selling it standalone.
signals.likelihood: Medium - no Cypriot enforcement signal; spend will ride the branch-automation cycle
signals.followup: Confirm the Cyprus law number and Official Gazette date from cylaw.org or the Deputy Ministry site, and whether a separate market-surveillance authority (e.g. Consumer Protection Service of the Ministry of Energy, Commerce and Industry) handles products/terminals as distinct from services - AccessibleEU only names the service-side authority.

signals.entity: European Commission (DG EMPL / infringement register)
signals.country: EU-wide (footprint: EL, CY, HR, SI, CZ)
signals.signal: VERIFIED NEGATIVE: the Commission's July 2026 infringement package (published 08/07/2026) contains NO European Accessibility Act / Directive (EU) 2019/882 decision at all - the only 'accessibility'-tagged reasoned opinions in that package concern Directive (EU) 2023/2661 on Intelligent Transport Systems (Belgium, Czechia, Ireland, Greece, Croatia, Cyprus, Luxembourg, Malta, Poland, Slovenia; INFR(2026)0054 Greece, INFR(2026)0074 Croatia, INFR(2026)0025 Cyprus, INFR(2026)0033 Czechia, INFR(2026)0142 Slovenia). The last EAA infringement step against a footprint state therefore remains the reasoned opinion to GREECE for incomplete transposition of Law 4994/2022, decided 12/03/2025 (formal notice 19/07/2022); no referral to the Court of Justice has been taken as of 08/07/2026.
signals.source_name: European Commission, 'July infringements package: key decisions', Brussels 08/07/2026 (inf-26-1376), full text read locally; and AccessibleEU (EC), 'The European Commission calls on Greece to fully transpose the EAA'
signals.implies: (a) AFFECTED: Greek banks (Alpha, NBG, Piraeus, Eurobank) operate under a framework the Commission still considers incompletely transposed - so the Greek rules can still TIGHTEN and a bank budgeting to today's minimum risks a second remediation. (b) MUST BUY/CHANGE: plan Greek ATM/terminal accessibility to EN 301 549 rather than to the current Greek text; maps to Printec x-core accessible UI and NCR ATM refresh in Greece. (c) BUDGET: no EU escalation means no hard new deadline - a watch item, but keep Greek fleet accessibility inside the normal ATM refresh cycle so it is not a separate later spend.
signals.likelihood: Low-Medium that the Commission refers Greece to the CJEU within 12 months; Medium that Greece amends Law 4994/2022
signals.followup: Monitor the autumn and December 2026 infringement packages for an EAA item and the FEK for a Greek amending law. Do NOT reuse aggregator claims that Bulgaria/Cyprus received EAA reasoned opinions in January 2026 - that did not survive checking against the primary package text.

signals.entity: Directorate for Safety and Compliance of Industrial Products, General Secretariat for Industry, Ministry of Development (Greek EAA market-surveillance authority for ATMs and payment terminals)
signals.signal: PRIMARY-TEXT CORRECTION of the baseline. Reading the Official Gazette text of Law 4994/2022 (FEK A' 215/18.11.2022) directly: Art.19(2)(a) designates the DIEFTHYNSI ASFALEIAS KAI SYMMORFOSIS VIOMICHANIKON PROIONTON (Directorate for Safety and Compliance of Industrial Products) of the General Secretariat for Industry, Ministry of Development and Investments, as the market-surveillance authority specifically for 'terminatika pliromon kai aftomates tameiakes michanes' (payment terminals and automated teller machines). EETT (the telecoms regulator) is competent ONLY for electronic-communications terminal equipment (Art.19(2)(b)) and for sanctions in electronic communications (Art.26(4)) - so the baseline's 'EETT enforces EUR 10k-100k' is WRONG for ATMs/POS. Art.26 as enacted contains NO monetary fine amounts at all: it provides only proportionality criteria and administrative MEASURES (recommendation for corrective action, temporary detention, prohibition of circulation/making available). Art.27(2) delegates the actual fine schedule for PRODUCTS to a future PRESIDENTIAL DECREE proposed jointly by the Ministers of Development, Finance, Digital Governance and Infrastructure & Transport; no such decree was found published as of 02/08/2026. Art.23 obliges banks and financial institutions to adapt processes and documents to Annex I Sections III, IV and VIII. Art.28(3): self-service terminals lawfully used before 28/06/2025 may run to end of economic life, max 20 years from first use; Art.28(1): services may use pre-existing products until 28/06/2030, and service contracts signed before 28/06/2025 survive unchanged for at most 5 years (i.e. to 28/06/2030).
signals.source_name: Efimerida tis Kyverniseos (Greek Official Gazette), Nomos 4994/2022, FEK A' 215/18.11.2022 - full PDF downloaded from et.gr and text-extracted locally (Arts.19, 23, 24, 26, 27, 28)
signals.implies: (a) AFFECTED: Alpha Bank, National Bank of Greece, Piraeus, Eurobank, Attica Bank, Optima, plus Euronet and Cardlink/Worldline as terminal deployers, and any VENDOR placing ATMs/POS on the Greek market - Printec itself is an 'economic operator' under Arts.7-10 and must hold EU declarations of conformity and technical documentation in Greek for every unit it supplies. (b) MUST BUY/CHANGE: because no fine schedule exists yet, the live Greek exposure is the ADMINISTRATIVE MEASURE - temporary detention or a ban on making a non-conformant terminal available, which would stop an ATM/POS rollout mid-deployment. Banks therefore need EN 301 549-evidenced conformity from their supplier, not a promise; maps to Printec NCR ATM supply with documented conformity, x-core accessible multivendor UI, Verifone/Castles accessible POS + TMS. Art.24 additionally bans charging consumers more for accessible access - so accessibility cost cannot be recovered from users. (c) BUDGET: the missing Presidential Decree is the thing to watch - once fines are quantified the Greek market moves fast; banks should have conformity assessment funded in the 2027 budget, decided H2-2026.
signals.likelihood: Medium that the Art.27(2) Presidential Decree issues within 12 months (the Commission's 12/03/2025 reasoned opinion on incomplete transposition pushes in that direction)
signals.followup: CORRECTS the baseline 'Greece Law 4994/2022 EUR 10k-100k (EETT)' - not supported by the enacted text; the EUR 10k-100k figure most likely belongs to a different Greek statute and should not be quoted for EAA. Monitor et.gr for the Art.27(1) joint ministerial decision (market-surveillance infrastructure and mixed inspection teams) and the Art.27(2) Presidential Decree on product fines; both are the missing pieces the Commission complained about. Printec's own conformity documentation obligations as an economic operator should be reviewed with Printec Legal/Compliance.

signals.entity: Slovenska obchodna inspekcia (SOI) - Slovak Trade Inspection Authority
signals.signal: PRIMARY-TEXT UPGRADE of the previous Low-confidence Slovak row. The consolidated Zbierka zakonov text of Act No. 351/2022 Z.z. (version effective 28/06/2025) confirms: SS8(1) makes the SLOVENSKA OBCHODNA INSPEKCIA the supervisory body for accessibility of SERVICES (including financial services and services delivered through interactive self-service terminals located in Slovakia), and SS9 makes SOI the supervisor for MAKING SPECIFIED PRODUCTS AVAILABLE ON THE MARKET under the conformity-assessment regime of Act 56/2018 Z.z. The Narodna banka Slovenska is NOT mentioned anywhere in the Act - unlike Croatia (HNB) and Hungary (MNB), Slovakia keeps accessibility entirely outside prudential supervision. SS10(2) fine schedule, now established from the primary text: EUR 200 up to 3% OF PRIOR-YEAR TURNOVER, capped at EUR 6,000 (failure to meet accessibility requirements or to publish accessibility information), EUR 20,000 (failure to have procedures, to notify the supervisor, or to take corrective action) and EUR 30,000 (failure to give SOI documentation/cooperation) - so the highest ceiling attaches to obstructing the inspector, not to the underlying inaccessibility. SS12(1) transition: a service supplied under a contract concluded on or before 28/06/2025 is exempt until the contract ends, at the latest 28/06/2030. The product-side accessibility requirements (including the 20-year self-service-terminal run-off) sit in a separate instrument, Government Regulation 282/2023 Z.z., not in Act 351/2022.
signals.source_name: Zbierka zakonov Slovenskej republiky - Zakon c. 351/2022 Z.z. o pristupnosti vyrobkov a sluzieb pre osoby so zdravotnym postihnutim, consolidated version effective 28/06/2025 (official PDF from slov-lex, text-extracted locally)
signals.implies: (a) AFFECTED: Slovenska sporitelna (Erste), VUB (Intesa), Tatra banka (RBI), CSOB SK, Postova banka, UniCredit SK, Prima banka, plus Euronet as an independent ATM deployer. (b) MUST BUY/CHANGE: the fine ceilings are small enough (EUR 6k-30k) that they will NOT by themselves fund an ATM refresh - the Slovak sales argument must therefore be the 28/06/2030 contract cut-off plus the SS7 obligation to hold a documented disproportionate-burden assessment, renewed every five years and producible to SOI on demand. That documentation requirement is a concrete, sellable deliverable: an EN 301 549 gap assessment of the ATM/POS estate, then remediation via x-core accessible multivendor UI and NCR ATM/recycler refresh, Verifone/Castles accessible POS + TMS. (c) BUDGET: assessment work 2026-2027; hardware/UI remediation must be contracted by 2028-2029 to clear 28/06/2030.
signals.likelihood: Medium - SOI has published no terminal-accessibility inspection results; the binding trigger is the 28/06/2030 contract cut-off rather than enforcement
signals.followup: CLOSES the baseline gap on Slovak fine levels (EUR 200 to 3% of turnover, capped 6,000/20,000/30,000) and CONFIRMS that NBS has no role. Next: pull Government Regulation 282/2023 Z.z. from slov-lex for the product-side technical requirements and the 20-year self-service-terminal derogation wording, and check SOI's annual report (soi.sk) for the first accessibility inspection statistics.

signals.entity: ETSI/CEN/CENELEC - EN 301 549 (harmonised standard for the EAA)
signals.country: EU-wide (footprint: AT, BG, HR, CY, CZ, EL, HU, RO, SK, SI)
signals.signal: MATERIAL CORRECTION OF A WIDELY REPEATED ASSUMPTION. Reading the ETSI deliverable text directly: the version of EN 301 549 currently in force, V3.2.1 (March 2021), was prepared under standardisation request C(2017)2585 and contains only Annex ZA, which maps to the WEB ACCESSIBILITY DIRECTIVE (Directive (EU) 2016/2102) - it contains NO Annex ZB and is NOT cited in the Official Journal under the European Accessibility Act. The first version prepared under the EAA standardisation request M/587 (Commission Implementing Decision C(2022)6456 final of 14/09/2022) is Draft EN 301 549 V4.1.0 (2025-11), which adds a new Annex ZB mapping to Directive (EU) 2019/882 and a new clause A.2 allowing conformance of specific ICT products and services to be evaluated against the EAA essential requirements. Its own Foreword states the presumption of conformity arises only 'once the present document is cited in the Official Journal of the European Union under that Directive'. As of 02/08/2026 V4.1.0 is still in the combined Public Enquiry and Vote phase of ETSI's Standardisation Request deliverable Approval Procedure (SRdAP); the final V4.1.1 and the OJ citation had not issued. Content changes: clauses 9, 10 and 11 realigned to WCAG 2.2, and real-time-text requirements in clause 6.2 significantly extended to total conversation. National transposition dates are relative, not absolute: announcement (doa) 3 months after ETSI publication, national publication/endorsement (dop/e) 6 months after doa, withdrawal of conflicting national standards (dow) 18 months after doa.
signals.source_name: ETSI/CEN/CENELEC, Draft EN 301 549 V4.1.0 (2025-11), Harmonised European Standard 'Accessibility requirements for ICT products and services' - PDF downloaded from the ETSI deliver repository with a desktop User-Agent and text-extracted locally (Foreword, Introduction, informative references [i.26]-[i.30])
signals.implies: (a) AFFECTED: every bank, acquirer and terminal deployer in the 10 EU footprint states, and Printec itself as an 'economic operator' placing ATMs and POS terminals on those markets. (b) MUST BUY/CHANGE: because no harmonised standard is yet cited in the OJ for the EAA, a supplier CANNOT today claim automatic presumption of conformity by invoking EN 301 549 - conformity must be self-declared against the Annex I essential requirements with its own technical documentation and EU declaration of conformity. That makes documented, test-evidenced accessibility conformance a genuine differentiator in ATM/POS tenders rather than a tick-box; maps to Printec NCR ATM supply with documented conformity files, x-core multivendor accessible UI (the cheapest way to bring a mixed legacy fleet to one evidenced UI baseline), Verifone/Castles accessible POS + TMS, and accessibility gap-assessment services. (c) BUDGET: when V4.1.1 is cited in the OJ, the WCAG 2.2 uplift in clauses 9-11 will re-open every bank's digital-channel and terminal-UI conformance evidence - banks should fund a re-assessment in the 2027 budget, decided H2-2026, and should require suppliers to commit contractually to V4.1.1 rather than V3.2.1.
signals.likelihood: Medium-High that V4.1.1 is finalised and cited in the OJ within 12 months; the vote phase is the last procedural step
signals.followup: CLOSES the baseline's loose statement that EAA conformance runs 'via EN 301 549 (incl. WCAG 2.1 AA)' - correct in substance but NOT via a cited harmonised standard, so there is no presumption of conformity today. Do NOT quote an OJ citation date: aggregator sources claim 'expected October 2026' but no primary source states it. Watch the OJ C series (harmonised standards under Directive (EU) 2019/882) and the ETSI work-item milestones page. Printec Legal/Compliance should review whether Printec's own EU declarations of conformity for ATMs/POS placed after 28/06/2025 reference the Annex I essential requirements directly.

signals.entity: Natsionalnyi bank Ukrainy (National Bank of Ukraine)
signals.signal: Ukraine has no EAA transposition (it is not an EU member and the EAA is not in the Association Agreement annexes), but the NBU regulates banking accessibility directly through the Regulation on Bank Licensing: banks must ensure PHYSICAL AND INFORMATIONAL accessibility of at least 50% of their separated subdivisions (branches) per region for people with disabilities, war veterans and older people, with a compliance date of 01/01/2025 and a continuing obligation thereafter; physical accessibility follows the state building standards on inclusivity of buildings, informational accessibility requires website and mobile-app information in a form usable by people with different functional impairments. NEW THIS PERIOD: by NBU Board Resolution No.81 of 15/07/2026 (amendments to the Regulation on financial monitoring by banks, in force 17/07/2026), the NBU widened permitted client identification/verification methods for financial-inclusion purposes - the original identity document may now be presented by an accompanying or trusted person, or with the assistance of the verifying bank employee, where the client cannot present it themselves, and consent to photo-capture may be evidenced by audio/video recording where a handwritten or electronic signature is impossible. The same resolution lets a 'financial inclusion bank' (a new institution type created by NBU Resolutions No.61, 64 and 65 of 12/06/2026, in force 26/06/2026) delegate identification and verification to commercial agents. The change followed a publicised case in which a quadruple-amputee veteran was refused a card at a PrivatBank branch because he could not hold the card to his face for photo verification. On the device side, Ukrainian press reports voice-assistant audio guidance installed on over 1,000 ATMs nationally and over 100 'Screen Switcher' rotating-screen adapters planned for installation on the self-service kiosks of two Ukrainian banks by 31/01/2026.
signals.source_name: National Bank of Ukraine, 'Rozshyreno perelik sposobiv veryfikatsii bankamy kliientiv dlia tsilei finansovoi inkliuzii' [The list of methods for bank verification of clients for financial-inclusion purposes has been expanded] - NBU news page fetched with a desktop User-Agent after a 403; branch 50% requirement from the NBU amendment to the Regulation on Bank Licensing as reported by Ukrinform; ATM device figures from Ekonomichna Pravda
signals.implies: (a) AFFECTED: PrivatBank (an existing Printec NCR recycler customer), Oschadbank, Raiffeisen Bank Ukraine, Universal Bank/monobank, PUMB, Ukrgasbank, Sense Bank, plus the new financial-inclusion bank type and its commercial agents. (b) MUST BUY/CHANGE: two distinct buys. First, branch and self-service accessibility retrofit - audio-guided ATM UI, headphone jack, tactile keypads, height/reach-compliant and rotatable screens - which Ukraine is buying NOW at scale because of ~94,000 war-related amputations in 2022-2024; maps to Printec NCR ATM/recycler supply, x-core accessible multivendor UI, self-service kiosks and field services. Second, assisted and agent-based onboarding - identification by a trusted third party, audio/video-evidenced consent, and agent-performed KYC - which maps directly to Printec digital onboarding/eKYC (Namirial) and AML/KYC (IMTF Siron, FICO), since the audio/video consent record and the agent chain must be captured, retained and made auditable. (c) BUDGET: the licensing 50% branch obligation is already live and continuing; the No.81 process change is in force since 17/07/2026 and banks must reconfigure onboarding flows immediately - this is an H2-2026 spend, not a 2027 one.
signals.likelihood: High - both obligations are in force; the financial-inclusion bank type creates a new agent-onboarding buyer within 6-12 months
signals.followup: Pull the consolidated text of NBU Resolution No.81 of 15/07/2026 and of Resolutions No.61/64/65 of 12/06/2026 from bank.gov.ua's Normatyvna baza (the NBU site 403s the fetch tool - use a desktop User-Agent). Confirm the exact NBU licensing-regulation resolution number and date behind the 50% branch requirement from the primary text rather than press. Approach PrivatBank and Oschadbank on accessible ATM UI + assisted-onboarding capture; approach the financial-inclusion bank promoters on agent eKYC.

signals.entity: European Commission, DG Enlargement - Serbia 2025 Report
signals.signal: The Commission's Serbia 2025 Report (SWD(2025) 755 final, Brussels 04/11/2025) states that Serbia's legal framework on the rights of persons with disabilities 'needs to be further aligned with the EU acquis and European standards, INCLUDING THE EUROPEAN ACCESSIBILITY ACT', and that enforcement mechanisms need to be improved; Serbia adopted a strategy and action plan in this area in January 2025. Serbia therefore has NO product-side accessibility law equivalent to Directive (EU) 2019/882 - no EAA-style conformity-assessment regime, no CE-style declaration for self-service terminals, and no designated market-surveillance authority for ATMs or payment terminals. The Narodna banka Srbije imposes no equivalent accessibility requirement on ATM or POS estates that could be identified from primary sources as of 02/08/2026. Accessibility obligations rest on the general anti-discrimination framework for persons with disabilities rather than on technical conformity of terminals.
signals.source_name: European Commission, Commission Staff Working Document 'Serbia 2025 Report', SWD(2025) 755 final, section on persons with disabilities - PDF downloaded from enlargement.ec.europa.eu and text-extracted locally
signals.implies: (a) AFFECTED: Banca Intesa Beograd, OTP banka Srbija, UniCredit Srbija, Raiffeisen banka Srbija (an existing Printec x-core customer), NLB Komercijalna, AIK Banka (an existing Printec NCR recycler customer), Erste Srbija. (b) MUST BUY/CHANGE: nothing is legally compelled today - so accessibility in Serbia is NOT a near-term spend trigger on its own. The realistic play is to attach accessible-UI and audio-guidance options to work Serbian banks are already funding for other reasons (SEPA SCT went operational 05/05/2026, ISO 20022 RTGS migration, recycler refresh), so the fleet is touched once. Parent-group policy is the second lever: Intesa, UniCredit, OTP, Erste, RBI and NLB all run EAA-conformant estates in their EU home markets and increasingly push group-wide device and UI standards into non-EU subsidiaries. Maps to x-core accessible multivendor UI, NCR ATM/recycler refresh, kiosks. (c) BUDGET: no regulatory deadline - budget will follow the group standard or the next hardware cycle, so sell into the 2027 fleet plan rather than to a compliance date.
signals.likelihood: Low that Serbia legislates an EAA-equivalent within 12 months; Medium that EU parent groups impose accessible-UI standards on Serbian subsidiaries in that window
signals.followup: Watch for a Serbian draft 'zakon o pristupacnosti proizvoda i usluga' in the Chapter 19/23 accession screening and in the Government's legislative plan; also check NBS's consumer-protection and payment-services regulations for any accessibility clause. Lead the commercial conversation with Raiffeisen Serbia and AIK Banka via the existing relationships, framed as group-standard alignment, not compliance.

signals.entity: European Commission, DG Enlargement - Montenegro 2025 Report
signals.signal: The Commission's Montenegro 2025 Report (SWD(2025) 754 final/2, Brussels 04/11/2025) finds that 'the legal and institutional framework for the rights of persons with disabilities is INCOMPLETE and needs to be further aligned with EU acquis, INCLUDING THE EUROPEAN ACCESSIBILITY ACT', that implementation and enforcement mechanisms need to be improved, and that some definitions in Montenegrin disability legislation use derogatory terminology. Montenegro is the most advanced footprint candidate (all 33 negotiating chapters opened) and is targeting accession, so an EAA-equivalent law is a foreseeable requirement - but none exists today and no market-surveillance authority for self-service terminals has been designated. This sits alongside Montenegro's live payments modernisation: the CBCG went live on the Western Balkans TIPS clone on 20/07/2026 with all 11 banks.
signals.source_name: European Commission, Commission Staff Working Document 'Montenegro 2025 Report', SWD(2025) 754 final/2, section on persons with disabilities - PDF downloaded from enlargement.ec.europa.eu and text-extracted locally
signals.implies: (a) AFFECTED: CKB (OTP), NLB Banka Podgorica, Erste Bank Montenegro, Hipotekarna banka, Universal Capital Bank, Adriatic Bank - all 11 CBCG-supervised banks. (b) MUST BUY/CHANGE: no product conformity obligation today. The concrete near-term work is the instant-payments/TIPS-clone rollout, and the accessibility argument is to specify accessible ATM/POS UI in that same refresh so the estate is EAA-ready before accession forces it; maps to Printec x-core accessible UI, NCR ATM refresh, POS + TMS. (c) BUDGET: tie to the 2026/2027 instant-payments and terminal refresh budget; there is no accessibility deadline to sell against.
signals.likelihood: Medium that Montenegro tables an EAA-equivalent bill within 24 months as an accession benchmark; Low within 12
signals.followup: Track the Montenegrin Ministry of Labour and Social Welfare legislative plan and the Chapter 19/23 action plans for an accessibility bill; re-read the 2026 enlargement package (expected autumn 2026) for movement.

signals.entity: Ministry of Digital Transformation / Sobranie - North Macedonia
signals.signal: North Macedonia legislated accessibility in 2025 but ONLY on the public-sector web side, not the EAA product side: the Law on Accessibility of Websites and Mobile Applications of Public Sector Institutions was published in Sluzben vesnik na Republika Severna Makedonija No.198 of 18/10/2025, requiring public-sector content to be perceivable through at least two different senses, all interactive elements operable regardless of input method, and content technically robust and compatible with assistive technologies - i.e. a transposition of the WEB ACCESSIBILITY DIRECTIVE (Directive (EU) 2016/2102), NOT of the European Accessibility Act. Banks, ATMs, payment terminals and consumer banking services are therefore OUT of scope; no North Macedonian law imposes EN 301 549-style conformity on self-service terminals and no market-surveillance authority has been designated for them. NBRM/NBRSM has published no accessibility requirement for ATM or POS estates identifiable from primary sources as of 02/08/2026.
signals.source_name: Ministry of Digital Transformation of the Republic of North Macedonia, press release on the new law making public-institution websites and mobile applications more accessible to persons with disabilities (Sluzben vesnik No.198, 18/10/2025)
signals.implies: (a) AFFECTED: Komercijalna banka Skopje, NLB Banka Skopje, Stopanska banka (OTP), Halkbank, ProCredit, Sparkasse Banka Makedonija - none currently under an EAA-equivalent terminal obligation. (b) MUST BUY/CHANGE: the sellable point is SEQUENCING. North Macedonia is mid-way through SEPA scheme adherence (operational readiness declared 05/10/2025) and is a candidate for the second Western Balkans TIPS-clone onboarding window expected November 2026; that programme touches the payments stack and the terminal estate. Specifying accessible ATM/POS UI now avoids a second, later, accession-driven retrofit; maps to Printec x-core accessible multivendor UI, NCR ATM refresh, POS + TMS. (c) BUDGET: rides the 2026/2027 instant-payments and SEPA budget - there is no accessibility budget line to target directly.
signals.likelihood: Low that an EAA-equivalent product law appears within 12 months; the web-accessibility law shows the legislature starts with the public sector
signals.followup: Obtain the Sluzben vesnik No.198/2025 text to confirm the law's exact title, scope and any private-sector extension clause, and check whether a follow-on EAA-equivalent bill is in the Government's 2026 legislative programme. Also check the NBRSM website for any accessibility guidance to banks.

signals.entity: European Commission, DG Enlargement - Bosnia and Herzegovina 2025 Report
signals.signal: The Commission's Bosnia and Herzegovina 2025 Report (SWD(2025) 751 final, Brussels 04/11/2025) finds the legal and institutional framework on the rights of persons with disabilities INCOMPLETE, with implementation and enforcement needing improvement and a lack of dedicated funds hindering progress; the country 'needs to align its legislation with the EU acquis, INCLUDING IN THE AREA OF ACCESSIBILITY'. Note that unlike the Serbia, Montenegro, Albania and Kosovo reports, the BiH text does NOT name the European Accessibility Act explicitly - it refers to accessibility acquis generically, which is a weaker and earlier-stage finding. BiH therefore has no EAA-equivalent product law, no conformity-assessment regime for self-service terminals and no designated market-surveillance authority for ATMs or payment terminals; the CBBH imposes no equivalent accessibility requirement identifiable from primary sources as of 02/08/2026. BiH's payments agenda is instead dominated by the Western Balkans TIPS clone, on which the CBBH went live as a co-first participant on 20/07/2026.

signals.implies: (a) AFFECTED: UniCredit Bank d.d. Mostar, Raiffeisen Bank BiH, Intesa Sanpaolo Banka BiH, NLB Banka Sarajevo/Banja Luka, ASA Banka, Addiko Bank. (b) MUST BUY/CHANGE: Nothing is legally compelled. The live spend is the TIPS-clone instant-payments rollout that went live 20/07/2026 and its terminal-side consequences; accessible ATM/POS UI should be specified into that same refresh so the estate is not touched twice. Maps to Printec x-core accessible multivendor ATM UI, NCR ATM/recycler refresh, self-service kiosks, Verifone/Castles accessible POS + TMS. (c) BUDGET: no accessibility deadline exists - budget will follow the payments/hardware cycle or an EU parent group's device standard, so specify accessible UI inside the next fleet or instant-payments tranche rather than selling accessibility standalone.

signals.entity: European Commission, DG Enlargement - Albania 2025 Report
signals.signal: The Commission's Albania 2025 Report (SWD(2025) 750 final, Brussels 04/11/2025) finds Albania's framework legislation on the rights of persons with disabilities only PARTIALLY COMPLIANT with the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, notes Albania has not ratified the UNCRPD Optional Protocol, and states that only limited action was taken to 'improve accessibility in line with the EU acquis, INCLUDING AS REGARDS THE EUROPEAN ACCESSIBILITY ACT'. Albania is the most exposed footprint candidate on timing because it is negotiating on an accelerated track and has already been admitted to SEPA (Albania, Moldova, Montenegro and North Macedonia joined the SEPA schemes in October 2025) and is expected in the second Western Balkans TIPS-clone onboarding window in November 2026. There is nonetheless no Albanian EAA-equivalent product law, no terminal conformity regime and no designated market-surveillance authority for ATMs/POS; Banka e Shqiperise has published no equivalent accessibility requirement identifiable from primary sources as of 02/08/2026.

Maps to Printec x-core accessible multivendor ATM UI, NCR ATM/recycler refresh, self-service kiosks, Verifone/Castles accessible POS + TMS. (c) BUDGET: no accessibility deadline exists - budget will follow the payments/hardware cycle or an EU parent group's device standard, so specify accessible UI inside the next fleet or instant-payments tranche rather than selling accessibility standalone.

signals.entity: European Commission, DG Enlargement - Kosovo 2025 Report

coverage_notes: Resumed from the 02/08/2026 partial checkpoint (12 signals kept unchanged: HU x2, HR, CZ, SI, AT, RO, BG, CY, EC-infringement, EL, SK) and researched ONLY the two items its 'remaining' note listed. GAP 1 - EN 301 549: CLOSED from the ETSI primary text. Material correction: the in-force V3.2.1 (Mar-2021) was made under standardisation request C(2017)2585 for the WEB ACCESSIBILITY DIRECTIVE and carries only Annex ZA; it has NO Annex ZB and is NOT cited in the OJ under Directive (EU) 2019/882, so there is currently NO harmonised standard conferring presumption of conformity for the EAA. Draft EN 301 549 V4.1.0 (2025-11), prepared under EAA standardisation request M/587 (C(2022)6456 final, 14/09/2022), is the first EAA version - it adds Annex ZB and clause A.2, realigns clauses 9-11 to WCAG 2.2 and extends clause 6.2 real-time text to total conversation, and as of 02/08/2026 is still in ETSI's combined Public Enquiry and Vote phase (SRdAP). No primary source states an OJ citation date; the widely repeated 'October 2026' is aggregator-only and is deliberately NOT quoted. GAP 2 - non-EU footprint: CLOSED for all seven. Ukraine researched from NBU primary (Regulation on Bank Licensing 50%-of-branches accessibility obligation from 01/01/2025; Board Resolution No.81 of 15/07/2026 in force 17/07/2026 widening identification/verification for clients who cannot present documents themselves; financial-inclusion bank created by Resolutions No.61/64/65 of 12/06/2026). Serbia, Montenegro, Albania and Kosovo each verified from the Commission's own 2025 country reports of 04/11/2025, which name the European Accessibility Act explicitly as an alignment gap (SWD(2025) 755, 754/2, 750, 752); Bosnia & Herzegovina (SWD(2025) 751) refers to the accessibility acquis generically WITHOUT naming the EAA - reported as the weaker finding it is. North Macedonia legislated only the public-sector web/mobile side (Sluzben vesnik 198, 18/10/2025 - a Web Accessibility Directive equivalent), leaving ATMs and payment terminals out of scope. VERIFIED NEGATIVE across all seven non-EU markets: no EAA-equivalent product law, no conformity-assessment regime for self-service terminals, and no designated market-surveillance authority for ATMs/POS as of 02/08/2026 - so accessibility is a fleet-cycle and parent-group-standard argument there, not a compliance deadline. Search angles used this run: English keyword search; EUR-Lex/EC harmonised-standards angle; ETSI deliver repository (direct PDF); EC enlargement country-report PDFs (six downloaded, five parsed); Ukrainian-language search («доступність банкоматів», «постанова НБУ», «фінансова інклюзія») plus the NBU's own Ukrainian news page; Serbian Cyrillic search («приступачност», «банкомати»); Macedonian search («Закон за пристапност») plus the Ministry of Digital Transformation's own Macedonian press page; Croatian/Bosnian search («zakon o pristupačnosti proizvoda i usluga»). GENUINE GAPS: (i) no primary OJ citation date for EN 301 549 V4.1.1 exists yet - nothing to find; (ii) the NBU's 50%-of-branches licensing amendment is cited via Ukrinform because the underlying NBU resolution number was not isolated this run; (iii) NBS, CBCG, CBBH, NBRSM, Bank of Albania and CBK news pages were not each individually swept for accessibility guidance - the EC country reports were used as the authoritative cross-country instrument instead, and each row's followup names the specific national page to sweep next run.
